title: Feed the App Its Environment
description: The app refuses to start because APP_ENV and API_PORT are unset; export them from .bashrc.
scenario: runapp.sh — the local app launcher — aborts with 'APP_ENV not set'. It sources ~/.bashrc and then requires two variables: APP_ENV (must be production) and API_PORT (must be 8443). Add both exports to /home/intern/.bashrc so every shell — and therefore the launcher — has them.
symptoms: The launcher sources ~/.bashrc before checking, so the fix belongs there
mission: Add `export APP_ENV=production` and `export API_PORT=8443` to /home/intern/.bashrc so runapp.sh starts successfully.

hints.title: export makes it visible
hints.content: A variable without export exists only in the current shell. Child processes (like runapp.sh) only see EXPORTED variables.

hints.title: Where to put it
hints.content: runapp.sh sources ~/.bashrc, so exports added there are picked up on its next run — no need to edit the launcher.

hints.title: Values or variables?
hints.content: `export APP_ENV=production` sets the literal string. Writing $APP_ENV=... would be an error — the dollar sign is only for READING variables.

acceptance_criteria.description: runapp.sh now starts and prints 'app starting in production on port 8443'
